forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.30. IMF PortWatch data (via MacroMicro) as of May 17 showed commercial transits at 2% of pre-crisis baseline — approximately 2 vessels against a pre-war ~95/day figure. Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, and Hapag-Lloyd remain suspended 'until further notice.' Lloyd's war-risk premium remains elevated at multi-percent of hull value; the LMA survey found 88% insurer appetite but safety-not-insurance is the binding constraint per LMA May statement. US Navy Operation Project Freedom paused May 6; only 2 US-flagged vessels escorted through as of that date. A US-Iran MOU remains unsigned as of May 27; without a signed instrument, Western shipping lines have no credible assurance to resume scheduled transits. The 50/day threshold requires roughly a 25x increase from current levels within 14 days — a near-zero base rate absent a deal closing before ~June 3.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (the operationally meaningful question is whether Western shipping has returned). PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels (Chinese, Indian, Turkish) transiting under Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing.

indicators.name: Lloyd's war-risk premium reduced below 1.5% of hull
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; insurance is the binding constraint on commercial transit.

indicators.name: Maersk/MSC/Frontline announce return to scheduled Hormuz transit
indicators.expected_effect: +25pp toward YES; major shipping lines lead the resumption.

A formal dissolution — if the bill completes three readings — would resolve this YES. However the bill still requires committee and two further plenary readings; no final vote has occurred. The probability will require cold-start reassessment at next Sunday audit given the material procedural advance.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: counts as YES (majority lost). If a single party (e.g. Smotrich) departs but coalition retains 61+: counts as NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas allowed per Codex DA #12.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.34. Trump publicly stated the deal was 'largely negotiated' (NPR, May 23). Rubio told reporters May 24 there was 'a pretty solid thing on the table' on Hormuz opening and a 'real significant time-limited negotiation on nuclear matters' (Al Jazeera, CNN). Iranian FM Araghchi and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf traveled to Doha May 25 to brief Qatar's leadership and examine frozen Iranian assets — including central bank chief Hemmati — a concrete sign of Iranian-side preparation for implementation (Al Arabiya, The National). The proposed MOU includes Hormuz full reopening during a 60-day final-negotiation window and Iran committing to no-nuclear-weapons pledge. Araghchi stated May 27 he was unsure whether a deal was imminent; Khamenei advisor Shamkhani dismissed US nuclear control demands as 'fantasy.' The gap on enrichment duration and on Hormuz tolls remains open per Iranian FM. A signed document has not been confirmed. Net: probability rises from 0.25 to 0.34, reflecting credible convergence but not a done deal.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal 'agreement in principle' does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; Araghchi/Ghalibaf in Doha May 25 for preparatory talks; direct Witkoff meeting not yet confirmed.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO at horizon. The US State Department did not withdraw sponsorship before EOD May 22 — it reconvened the security track at the Pentagon on May 29 and the political track on June 2-3, maintaining active sponsorship (CNBC, PBS, Sputnik/GlobalSecurity). The Lebanese government did not declare the truce void. IDF strikes in southern Lebanon continued through May 22 (Soufan Center May 22, Al Jazeera), including the killing of six paramedics, and Hezbollah fired rockets in retaliation, but neither party nor the US formally declared the ceasefire void. The resolution_criteria required a formal US or Lebanese government statement, which was not issued.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate within 72h of ceasefire extension
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.name: Hezbollah rocket barrage >50/day from south Litani
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The institutional structure is in place and both sides have accepted the format. The residual risk is escalation in southern Lebanon — IDF strikes continued through May 26 and Hezbollah retaliated — that could prompt a last-minute Israeli or Lebanese delegation withdrawal. Base rate for scheduled Pentagon-hosted security talks proceeding as announced, given the US's active sponsorship role, is high.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if US Defense Dept, Israeli government, or Lebanese government confirms the security meeting convened on or before May 29 with both Israeli and Lebanese military delegations. NO if meeting is postponed, cancelled, or held without one of the two delegations.

Meeting postponed by <48h but still held in the same week = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-YES if both delegations ultimately present. One-sided attendance = RESOLVED-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran sign or publicly co-confirm any written instrument (MOU, framework, ceasefire extension, or equivalent) before EOD 2026-06-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The current diplomatic track is at its most advanced point since the war began: Trump said the deal is 'largely negotiated' (NPR, May 23); Rubio confirmed 'a pretty solid thing on the table' (Al Jazeera, May 24); Araghchi and Ghalibaf flew to Doha May 25 to brief Qatar and examine Iranian frozen assets (Al Arabiya, The National), consistent with Iranian-side pre-implementation preparation. The Axios May 24 report described the proposed one-page MOU's core terms (Hormuz reopening, 60-day negotiation window, no-nuclear-weapons pledge, sanctions-relief commitment). However, Araghchi said May 27 he was unsure a deal was imminent; Shamkhani dismissed nuclear-control terms as 'fantasy.' The 7-day window is tight. Probability 0.38 reflects a genuine coin-flip between the pace of convergence and the documented enrichment/tolls sticking points.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any written instrument between the US and Iran is publicly confirmed by both a named US official and a named Iranian official by EOD 2026-06-03, regardless of label (MOU, framework, ceasefire extension, letter of intent). NO if no such co-confirmation occurs by that date.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Axios, Reuters, or AP citing named US principal (Trump/Rubio/Witkoff) AND named Iranian principal (Pezeshkian/Araghchi) confirming the same document. Official State Dept or Iran MFA press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral US claim without Iranian confirmation = NOT resolved YES. Iranian counter-proposal without US acknowledgment = NOT resolved YES. Verbal 'agreement in principle' by envoys without principal confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire (extended May 15, running to approximately June 29) remain formally intact — with both US sponsorship and Lebanese government adherence maintained — through EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. The Lebanon ceasefire did not formally collapse by its May 22 test (F4 resolved NO). The US-sponsored security track reconvenes at the Pentagon May 29; political talks scheduled June 2-3. Both the US and Lebanon have maintained formal sponsorship through May 26. However, IDF strikes in southern Lebanon killed at least 657 people since the ceasefire, including six paramedics on May 22; Hezbollah has fired rockets in response; Ben-Gvir called for 'large-scale combat' May 25; and the Washington Post (May 26) reported the ceasefire 'faltering.' The question is whether the formal framework — defined as US sponsorship + Lebanese government adherence — survives to June 10. The Pentagon track May 29 and political track June 2-3 create institutional lock-in for at least the next 14 days, raising probability. But the escalatory environment on the ground is the key risk.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both US sponsorship (no State Dept withdrawal statement) and Lebanese government formal adherence are maintained through EOD 2026-06-10. NO if the US State Department withdraws sponsorship OR the Lebanese FM/PM publicly declares the truce void before that date.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept named spokesperson or press release; Lebanese PM or FM statement quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP. Silence (no withdrawal statement from either party) resolves YES.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon without US State Dept withdrawal = NOT collapse (ceasefire is acknowledged porous). Hezbollah rocket fire without Lebanese FM declaration = NOT collapse. Only a formal US or Lebanese government withdrawal statement triggers NO resolution.

indicators.name: Pentagon security track convenes as scheduled May 29 with both Israeli and Lebanese military delegations
indicators.expected_effect: +12pp toward YES; scheduled institutional engagement is anti-collapse signal.
